note: Measured, not aspirational. On 2026-08-22, after the language booster was narrowed to prose, '+'-as-space form encoding was decoded inside URL query components, the tool-invocation rule was split so a Markdown shell fence is recorded but not scored, and role reassignment gained a line-initial imperative net, the shipped engine (configs/default-rules.json + the default detector registry) scored 44/44 = 100% detection and 1/21 = 4.7619% false positives on this corpus. The floor is that detection rate rounded DOWN to 4dp and the ceiling that FP rate rounded UP to 4dp, so the gate cannot fail against the run that set it -- and nothing looser: one missed malicious case takes detection to 43/44 = 97.73% (fails), one more quarantined benign case takes FP to 2/21 = 9.52% (fails). A detection floor of 1.0 is only honest while no same-class bypass is known to be passing outside the corpus; it read 1.0 once when that was not true, which is why the 'laundered' class now exists. The single remaining false positive is security-advisory-quoting-injection, and it is a deliberate, permanent gap rather than an unfinished one: it is paired with laundered-advisory-prose, which is the SAME PROSE with a live payload substituted for the quoted one. Both score 1.00 on the same signal; one wants pass and one wants quarantine. Every content-only discriminator that passes the advisory therefore passes a working injection -- quotation containment, defensive-context markers and payload density were each prototyped and measured, and each is forgeable for between 2 and 138 bytes. Do not 'fix' it: the laundered class exists so that attempting to will turn this gate red, which is the correct outcome. Move these numbers only after measuring a real change, and say so in CHANGELOG.md. Tightening them is the point; loosening them to make a red build green is how a gate stops meaning anything.
